children: U.S. stocks are rebounding from a sell-off driven by the Fed's interest rate hike and high fuel prices. Major indexes are higher today: The Nasdaq is up around 1.5%, the S&P 500 gained 1% and the Dow industrials rose 0.5%.
Here's what is moving markets today:

The interest rate hike aftermath: Stocks and bonds stumbled following the Fed's decision to raise interest rates by a quarter point to between 3.75% and 4%. But markets are reversing course Thursday to pre-FOMC levels.

Tech stocks: The tech sector gained broadly Thursday, with Magnificent Seven companies and semiconductors leading. Intel and IonQ climbed more than 8%. The iShares semiconductor index rose more than 3%.
Oil prices: Fuel prices fell on hopes that damage to a Saudi pipeline might not be as severe as initially feared. Brent crude fell around 2% to below $104 after reaching $109 earlier this week.
This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
